scenes.title: Twenty Paces East
scenes.summary: Outside the courtyard gate on {STREET}, F1, M2, and M3 check the brass compass and count twenty paces east toward the stone fountain.
scenes.intro: Mid-morning sunlight warms the cobblestones of {STREET} in {CITY}. Stepping through the open courtyard gate of {SHOW}, {F1} holds the brass pocket compass steady while {M2} and {M3} examine Clue Card One. Listen first.
story: F1
What a glorious Saturday morning for a treasure walk down {STREET}!
M3
Let us check the brass compass first: east runs straight toward the corner bakery.
M2
Read Clue Card One aloud, {F1}, so we do not miss a single word.
F1
Card One says: Twenty paces east where cool clear water greets the morning birds.
M2
Easy! That is the little carved stone fountain at the end of our block!
M3
Wait, {M2}—whose paces are we counting, yours or mine?
F1
Good question, because {M2} walks like he is chasing a departing bus!
M2
Very funny, {F1}; let us walk side by side at a polite normal step.
M3
Five, ten, fifteen... eighteen, nineteen, and twenty paces right to the kerb!
F1
Look ahead—two sparrows are splashing on the rim of the stone fountain!
M2
Thirty years later, the morning birds are still keeping their appointment!
M3
Now look closely at Card One to see what symbol we need to find.
scenes.outro: Twenty steady paces east bring {F1}, {M2}, and {M3} straight to the sunlit stone fountain on {STREET}. See you next time.

scenes.title: By the Stone Fountain
scenes.summary: At the neighbourhood stone fountain, F1 and M3 spot a carved leaf pointing toward the clock tower, but M2 insists on taking a back-lane shortcut.
scenes.intro: Clear water trickles gently into the carved limestone basin on {STREET}. {F1} and {M3} compare the watercolour card with the stone rim while {M2} peers eagerly down a narrow side lane. Let us listen in first.
story: F1
Look at the left side of the watercolour sketch—there is a tiny carved leaf!
M3
Walk around the dry side of the basin, {F1}; do you see it on the stone?
F1
Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
M3
Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
F1
Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
M2
Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
M3
Are you sure about this narrow lane, {M2}? My compass says that bends south.
M2
I have lived on {STREET} for twenty years, {M3}, and alleys beat compasses!
F1
Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, {M2}?
M2
Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighbourhood lane?
M3
All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
F1
Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence—where are we going?!
scenes.outro: Ignoring both the brass compass and his own reading glasses, {M2} marches everyone proudly down a winding side alley. See you next time.

scenes.title: The Famous Shortcut
scenes.summary: After three confident left turns, M2 leads the group straight back outside F2's open café kitchen window at {SHOW}.
scenes.intro: Five minutes and three confident turns later, {M2} rounds a sunny brick corner expecting the municipal clock tower—and stops right underneath the open café window of {SHOW}, where {F2} is dusting warm rolls with cinnamon. Listen first.
story: M2
Aha! Behold this quiet historic wall—we must be right behind the clock square!
F2
Good morning again, boss! Did you forget your wallet, or did you miss me?
M2
{F2}?! Why are you standing inside a window behind the municipal clock tower?!
F1
Because three left turns make a circle, {M2}, and this is our own kitchen window!
F2
Wait—tell me you took your famous back-alley shortcut without your glasses again!
M2
Someone clearly moved that green garden fence since last spring!
F1
Look on the bright side: nobody gets hungry on a circular expedition!
F2
Here, take three warm cinnamon rolls in a paper bag before you try again.
M2
Thank you, {F2}, and please do not mention a single word of this to {M1}.
F2
My lips are sealed, provided you follow {M3} and the brass compass from here!
F1
Deal! Hand over command of the map cards, {M2}, before twelve noon strikes!
M2
Very well, walk straight up {STREET}—I was merely testing your sense of direction!
scenes.outro: Armed with warm cinnamon rolls and humble pie, the crew sets off again—this time following the brass compass up {STREET}. See you next time.

scenes.title: Shadow of the Clock Tower
scenes.summary: Joined by M4 at the municipal clock tower at noon, F1 and M3 watch the tower shadow point straight to a carved compass stone.
scenes.intro: At five minutes to twelve, {F1} and {M3} reach the sunny municipal clock tower square while {M2} catches his breath on a step nearby. {M4} waves warmly as he walks over on his Saturday errand break. Listen first.
story: M4
{F1}! {M3}! What brings our courtyard crew up to the clock tower square?
F1
We are following thirty-year-old map clues from a tin box under our courtyard tree!
M3
You arrived at the exact right minute, big brother—watch the tall clock hands above.
M4
One minute to twelve... listen, there goes the first deep bronze chime!
F1
Card Two says: Stand where the noon shadow touches a stone star on the ground.
M3
Follow the dark tip of the tower shadow across the paving stones with me!
M4
Right here beside the lamppost base—someone carved a small four-point star!
F1
And look at the arrow on the longest point of the star—it aims back south!
M3
What does Clue Card Three say about heading south toward the middle of {STREET}?
F1
Where second-hand stories sleep beneath a cool stone arch, look up at eye level!
M4
That is definitely the old second-hand bookshop with the arched stone doorway!
M3
Let us collect {M2} and {F3}—the bookshop arch is only four minutes away!
scenes.outro: Twelve noon chimes ring out across {CITY}, and the clock tower shadow points our team straight toward the second-hand bookshop arch. See you next time.

scenes.title: Under the Bookshop Arch
scenes.summary: Meeting F3 under the stone arch of the second-hand bookshop, F1 spots the green lending shelf in Card Three—making F3 gasp as she remembers the botanical book in Room 4.
scenes.intro: Halfway back down {STREET}, {F3} steps out from browsing sheet music under the cool stone arch of the neighbourhood second-hand bookshop just as {F1} hurries up holding Clue Card Three. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: F3
There you are, {F1}! I walked up from {SHOW} hoping to meet your clue hunt!
F1
You picked the exact right spot, {F3}—this stone arch IS Clue Card Three!
F3
Let me see the watercolour drawing: there is the arched doorway and the wooden cart!
F1
Read the line underneath: Beside the green lending shelf, four corners wait to meet.
F3
Wait a moment... look at that little green wooden shelf painted on the left wall!
F1
Yes! Free Neighbourhood Herb and Garden Books—why are you smiling like that, {F3}?
F3
Good heavens, {F1}, on Thursday afternoon I borrowed an old green leaf book from here!
F1
NO WAY! An old green cloth book of garden leaves—is it upstairs in Room Four?!
F3
Sitting right beside my teacup on the windowsill, and I have not finished reading it yet!
F1
Do you think the missing half of the berry cake recipe is tucked inside?!
F3
We will check every single page the moment we finish Clue Card Four!
F1
Look at the brass plaque above the shelf—an arrow pointing to the park bench!
scenes.outro: Under the cool bookshop arch, {F3} realises the mysterious green book of garden leaves might already be waiting upstairs in Room 4! See you next time.

scenes.title: The Shaded Park Bench
scenes.summary: At the shaded public garden bench at the end of {STREET}, M3 places all four square cards together to reveal a bird's-eye map of {SHOW} with a red star on the upper balcony.
scenes.intro: Under leafy trees at the quiet public garden at the end of {STREET}, {F1}, {M3}, and {M2} gather around a green wooden park bench to read the fourth and final watercolour card. Let us listen in first.
story: M2
Ah, a comfortable wooden bench in the shade—my feet approve of Clue Four!
F1
Listen to the final rhyme: Sit in the shade and bring all four corners home together.
M3
Bring all four corners together... hand me Cards One, Two, and Three, {F1}!
M2
Wait—look at the faint blue lines drawn along the outer edges of each card!
M3
Turn them face up on the flat bench slat like four tiles of one square...
F1
Card One top left, Card Two top right, Card Three bottom left, Card Four bottom right!
M2
Incredible! Together the four backs form a bird-eye drawing of {SHOW}!
M3
There is our courtyard tree, there are the arched windows of Room Nine...
F1
And look up on the second-floor wooden courtyard balcony—a bright red painted star!
M2
Why did the mapmaker paint a red star on our upstairs courtyard balcony?!
M3
Perhaps the small wax-sealed envelope in your pocket has the answer, {F1}!
F1
We walked every clue honestly—even {M2} and his extra circle—so let us open it!
scenes.outro: Placed edge to edge on the shaded park bench, the four cards unite into a secret map of {SHOW} crowned with a bright red star. See you next time.

scenes.title: Opening the Small Envelope
scenes.summary: On the park bench, F1, F3, and M3 break the wax seal and read the mapmaker's promise to return for Saturday tea thirty summers later.
scenes.intro: {F3} sits beside {F1} and {M3} on the sunlit garden bench as {F1} gently lifts the thirty-year-old red wax seal on the small square envelope. Listen first.
story: F3
Open the flap gently, {F1}; that little envelope has waited patiently since May.
F1
Inside is a folded ivory note card written in the same crisp mapmaker ink!
M3
Please read every word aloud for us, {F1}.
F1
Dear Friends of {STREET}, if you are sitting on our favourite park bench today...
F3
Then Room Nine has opened its green shutters to the neighbourhood once more!
F1
Listen to the next line: Thirty summers ago, five friends made a Saturday promise.
M3
What promise did my professor and the courtyard crew make back then, {F1}?
F1
To hang lanterns from the red-star balcony and share berry almond cake again!
F3
Oh, how lovely—and is there a postscript at the bottom of the card?
M3
Look: Watch your front-desk mail this week, because I keep my promises!
F1
Wait—he already mailed that first postcard from abroad two weeks ago!
M3
What if a second message arrived at {SHOW} while we were out walking?!
scenes.outro: The thirty-year promise is clear: balcony lanterns, summer berry cake, and a mapmaker who always keeps his word! See you back at the front desk next time.

scenes.title: Message at the Front Desk
scenes.summary: Returning briskly to the front desk, F1 and M2 find M1 holding an express station message announcing the retired mapmaker arrives next Saturday evening.
scenes.intro: Ten minutes later, {F1} and {M2} hurry back through the courtyard gate into the cool front lobby, where {M1} stands behind the desk tapping a yellow express envelope against his paper ledger. Listen first.
story: M1
You took your time—did the boss try his famous alley shortcut past the kitchen?
M2
Never mind the route, {M1}! What is that yellow envelope in your hand?!
M1
Express station post, signed for at eleven-forty while you were chasing clock shadows.
F1
Look at the sender line on the left—it is from our Room Eight mapmaker!
M2
Open it, {F1}, open it before my glasses fall right off my nose!
F1
Arriving in {CITY} next Saturday for the thirtieth May anniversary at {SHOW}!
M2
Next Saturday?! The original guest from Room Eight is coming HERE in person?!
M1
Read the last line at the bottom—that is the part for the kitchen.
F1
Hoping with all my heart to taste one slice of that famous berry almond cake!
M2
Merciful heavens, we still only have the TOP HALF of that cake recipe!
M1
Better go ask {F3} about that old green garden book in Room Four right now.
F1
Up the stairs we go—next Saturday is seven days away, and the oven awaits!
scenes.outro: The retired mapmaker arrives next Saturday in person—hoping for a cake whose second half is still missing! End of Episode 2—see you in Episode 3!
